{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** Legal (In-House Counsel)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings  
**Party posture:** We represent the Customer.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against nineteen playbook rules. The document is, on the whole, strongly customer-favourable: seventeen of nineteen rules are compliant, several of them above our preferred position. In particular, the IP and deliverables package (§ 14), the perpetual paid-up licence grant (§ 13), Vendor indemnification sitting outside the liability cap (§ 20, § 21.3), unqualified termination for convenience on thirty days' notice (§ 9.4, § 29.4), the six-month transition assistance and data-return regime (§ 11), New York law and venue (§ 28), and the absence of any exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-commitment obligation on us all meet or exceed our preferred positions.

Two issues require negotiation, and both fall into walk-away territory under the playbook:

1. **Liability cap is illusory (§ 21, critical).** The cap is keyed to "Fees," which is defined in §§ 1.5–1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The twelve-month look-back therefore captures no subscription or services charges, leaving a cap far below six months of actual fees. The mutuality, the § 21.2 exclusion of indirect damages and the § 21.3 carve-outs are all acceptable — the defect is the cap basis alone.

2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment (§ 7.7, high).** Liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, fail both our preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). The compounding weekly charge can exceed remaining contract value on a minor breach.

We recommend advancing two targeted redlines and closing on the remainder as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Cap keyed to Fees (one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee per §§ 1.5–1.6); illusory cap, walk-away territory. Carve-outs and mutuality compliant. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week on a ten-day delay; fails preferred and fallback; walk-away territory. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Meets preferred; indemnity is an Excluded Claim under § 21.3, so uncapped (better than fallback super-cap). |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables | Meets preferred in full; Deliverable ownership conditioned on payment and telemetry carve-out noted, both customary. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | Meets preferred; § 24.4 bars Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No exclusivity on us; § 12.4 restraint runs in our favour. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence | Above fallback: Affiliate and contractor use without notice gating; perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination (§ 9.4; § 29.4) | 30 days' notice, accrued Fees only, prepaid Fees refunded; Vendor has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights | Meets preferred on all material terms; no direct system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law and New York County exclusive jurisdiction; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) | Only MFN language runs in our favour; retain as drafted. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope (§ 2.1) | No minimum commitment; reinforced by §§ 7.1, 8.2, 12.3. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities (§ 12.3) | No no-hire or no-poach covenant on either Party. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal (§§ 8.2–8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Up to six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; deletion only after confirmed return. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties | Meets preferred; Hosted Services warranted for the subscription term; disclaimer does not swallow express warranties. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | Meets preferred; USD 5M cyber/privacy given Vendor hosts Customer Data. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

Both deviations are identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 21 — Illusory liability cap.** A cap limited to the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee leaves us without meaningful recourse for capped claims. Our position: the cap must be keyed to all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor. The existing § 21.2 exclusions and § 21.3 carve-outs remain untouched.

2. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** A compounding weekly charge of 15% of annual Fees, triggered by a ten-day delay, is a penalty we cannot accept. Our position: delete the liquidated damages and substitute customary simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, preserving our § 7.3 withholding right.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. Issue the two redlines to Vendor: (a) § 21 cap replacement — greater of twelve months of amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000; and (b) § 7.7 deletion with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts substituted.
2. Accompany each redline with a short cover note citing the playbook position and, on the cap, noting that the defect is the definition of "Fees" in §§ 1.5–1.6 rather than the structure of § 21 — this should be an easy fix for Vendor.
3. Confirm with the deal team the expected annual contract value so we can validate that the USD 1,000,000 floor is the right number for this deal.
4. Close on all seventeen compliant items as drafted; no further redlines are required, and we should resist reopening provisions that currently run in our favour (§§ 7.6, 12.4).
5. Escalate to the business sponsor only if Vendor refuses either walk-away item.
"}
